loops.name: Evidence and final handoff

checks.question: Machine-validate JSON, unique IDs, mappings, source references, example coverage and evidence lines.
Attach the independent page-by-page rule-review ledgers maintained by the other reviewers.
Separate source review, synthetic browser checks, native live checks and assistive-technology checks.
State untested native domains and that no live mutation or build was performed in this audit.
Record accepted, rejected or deferred proposal decisions without silently marking them implemented.
checks.result: All 44 items remain proposed/open. Acceptance and implementation decisions are future work, not failed audit steps.

repeatWhen: A proposed change is approved, implemented or released.

stopConditions: Do not infer compliance with unfinished or unreviewed guidelines.
Do not label native Home Assistant functionality missing because a civica guide is absent.
Do not treat a locally working specimen as a connected backend.
Do not change published URLs or runtime behaviour during an audit-only task.
completionDefinition: Requirements and taxonomy review complete; root integrates independent per-page ledgers and rendered validation separately. Proposals remain open until approved work meets their acceptance criteria.

guidanceReview.result: Proposed requirements and taxonomy were checked against the frozen rule scopes. Relevant rule dependencies are attached to every proposal. This is not a pass for existing component implementation or live Home Assistant.
scopeCautions: Writing requirements apply to civica-authored strings, not wholesale rewriting of native translations or user names.
Illustration restrictions do not remove functional icon strokes, chart patterns or operational imagery.
New-artwork rules do not automatically establish a MUST violation in pre-existing promotional artwork.
Native source presence, reference examples and implemented private adapters remain separate coverage categories.

remediation.scope: Canonical documentation/navigation, complete specifications and synthetic browser acceptance; native task and live equipment acceptance remain separate.
